# The monthly pay app, without the spreadsheet scramble.

PayApps is a hosted pay-application tool for subcontractors: your schedule of values, retainage, change orders and lien waivers in one place, so each month's pay app is a review instead of a rebuild.

[Start free on one job](https://payapps.marisstella.app/?signup&from=payapps-site) [See what it does](https://marisstella.app/payapps/features)

Worked example Application #2, period to Oct 31 · a made-up electrical job

LineScheduledComplete

1 Rough-in, floors 1–2
$84,000.00
70%

2 Switchgear and panels
$62,000.00
50%

3 Lighting fixtures
$41,000.00
30%

4 Trim, test and close-out
$23,000.00
0%

Completed and stored to date$102,100.00

Retainage held (10%)−$10,210.00

Less previous certificates−$52,560.00

Current payment due$39,330.00

Figures computed by the same pay-app math the app runs. Line 3's fixtures are stored on site, not yet installed: they count toward the total and carry retainage.

## What billing day looks like for a lot of subs

If you bill general contractors on a schedule of values, this list will be familiar. Every item is a place for a number to go wrong, and a wrong number can mean the pay app comes back and payment slips to the next cycle.

### Schedule of values

Percent complete on every line, work completed this period, materials stored, and totals that must match the GC's copy of your SOV to the cent.

### Retainage

Withheld on every line, sometimes at a different rate on stored materials or after a project milestone, depending on the contract. Tracking what is owed back across jobs is its own spreadsheet.

### Change orders

Approved changes become new SOV lines; pending ones usually can't be billed yet. Keeping both lists straight with the GC is a monthly back-and-forth.

### Lien waivers

A conditional waiver for this payment, an unconditional one for the last, sometimes on a form your state prescribes, sometimes notarized, and the same again from your suppliers.

### GC portals

Every general contractor has its own portal, cut-off date, required attachments and format. The numbers get typed in again, once per GC.

### QuickBooks

Then the same amounts go into your accounting system as invoices, with retainage receivable tracked separately, so the books match what you billed.

## How PayApps works

- **Set up a job once.** Import the schedule of values from your own spreadsheet or the PDF bid breakdown, with the contract sum, retainage rate and pay terms. Already billing the job? Start from your last application.

- **Update progress each month.** Work this period and stored materials per line; the continuation-sheet math, retainage and "less previous certificates" are calculated for you.

- **Send it with its backup.** The application and continuation sheet as PDF and CSV for the GC's portal or email, the waiver it needs, and the backup attached.

- **Get paid and keep the books straight.** Record each check, see what is past due across every job, send the invoice and payment to QuickBooks Online, and bill the retainage when the work is done, with the punch items and close-out documents it still waits on named job by job.

All four steps work in the app today. The [features page](https://marisstella.app/payapps/features) marks what is built and what comes next.

## Questions

### Can I use PayApps today?

Yes. PayApps is open: sign up with your email and set up your first job. Free on one job with no card. Paid plans for more jobs are not on sale yet. It is new, so there are no customer reviews yet; tell us what gets in your way.

### Who is PayApps for?

Subcontractors and specialty trades who bill general contractors every month with a schedule of values, retainage and lien waivers: electrical, mechanical, plumbing, framing, drywall, concrete, roofing and similar trades.

### Does it replace my GC's billing portal?

No. Your GC decides how pay apps are submitted. It keeps your numbers and backup in one place and gives you the PDF and CSV, so the portal step is copying finished figures, not redoing them. For Procore, Oracle Textura, GCPay and Trimble Pay it also fills the SOV and billing files those portals take; you still submit them in the portal yourself.

### Is it an AIA G702/G703 form?

Features

# What PayApps does

Items marked **Built · in testing** work in the app today. Items marked **Next** are planned, not built; the subcontractors using it set their order.

Built · in testing

## Schedule of values per job

Each job starts from the SOV in your subcontract, with the contract sum and retainage terms. Every pay app is built from it, so lines, scheduled values and totals stay the same from month to month, and the SOV locks once the first pay app goes out.

- Import your own .xlsx, CSV or PDF bid breakdown (a PDF printed from Excel or an estimating program, or a scan: a searchable PDF's text layer is read, and a scan of pictures only, even one fed in sideways or upside down, is read by OCR in your browser, up to ten pages, with a note to check it against the paper): the file is read in your browser and never uploaded, title blocks, division headings, subtotals and totals are left out (each listed with its row), and the sheet's own total is checked against its lines and the contract sum
- Or paste rows from Excel or Google Sheets, copy another job's lines, or type them in
- Starting mid-job? Enter your last application from the old spreadsheet or software as the opening balance and carry on from the next number
- GC on Procore asking for a detailed subcontractor SOV? Choose the CSV template the GC's commitment gives you, place each of your lines under one of their positions, see the totals against theirs, and download the filled template to import; save the placement with the job for the monthly Procore invoice. Columns and the GC's cells are kept as they are; built from Procore's published instructions, not yet tried on a live Procore project
- GC on GCPay asking for your schedule of values breakdown? Download it as the Excel file GCPay's Upload button takes (Item Number, Description and Value, base contract only, as GCPay's subcontractor guide sets out), with a check that the lines add up to the contract amount before GCPay refuses the submission. Built from GCPay's published subcontractor guide, not yet tried on a live GCPay project
- Unit-price contracts: give a line its quantity, unit and unit price (3,400 LF of curb at $18.25) and bill it each month by the quantity installed. The dollars are always quantity × unit price to the cent, the quantity to date is on the screen, the CSV and the PDF, and GCPay's five-column unit-price SOV (Units, Unit Description, Unit Value) downloads from the same job

Built · in testing

## The monthly pay app

Enter work completed this period and materials presently stored per line; the continuation-sheet columns follow: total completed and stored, percent complete, balance to finish and retainage.

- GC billing through Procore? Each pay app has a Procore invoice sheet: the Work Completed This Period and materials-stored amounts to type into the GC's Procore invoice, line by line, with copy buttons, so it matches the G702/G703 you send. If the GC's invoice lists their own SOV positions instead of your lines, save where your lines sit under those positions once (from the subcontractor SOV template) and every pay app's sheet totals by position, with change orders listed apart. Where the stored-materials balance fell and new deliveries can't be told apart, it says so instead of guessing. Built from Procore's published help, not yet tried on a live Procore project
- GC billing through Oracle Textura? Download the This Period or To Date billing template from Textura's Upload Billing Amounts, choose it on the pay app, and download it back filled: Work This Period and Material Stored This Period, or Completed to Date (work completed plus materials stored, G703 column G), on each of your lines, matched by phase code, description or budget (change any match), with every other cell kept as Textura wrote it, ready for the same upload. Lines on no Textura row, budgets that differ from your SOV, and To Date lines where Textura already shows more than your application are pointed out. Built from Oracle's published help, not yet tried on a live Textura project
- Summary page: original contract sum, net change by change orders, total completed and stored to date, retainage, less previous certificates, current payment due
- PDF in a familiar application-and-continuation-sheet layout (our own layout, not an AIA document), plus CSV
- Draft, submitted, certified and paid, with the GC's certified amount where it differs; history that can't be rewritten
- Lender, title company or owner asking for a contractor's sworn statement (the Illinois and Michigan kind)? The job's sworn statement page lists everyone who supplied labor or material, prefilled from its purchase orders and subcontracts, checked against the contract sum and the pay app's amount due, and prints as a PDF with a jurat for the notary. Which statement a draw needs, and whether it is complete, is yours to check
- GC wants it notarized? Turn on the notary block for that job and the summary page carries a jurat with blanks and a seal box under your signature
- Attach the backup to each pay app: stored-material invoices, certified payroll, insurance certificates, photos, the signed copy the GC returns
- Keep your certificates of insurance (general liability, auto, workers' comp, umbrella and others) with their policy dates: a note on the projects page 30 days before one expires, and a warning on any draft pay app dated on or after an expiry, or within 30 days before it, so a lapsed certificate doesn't hold up the payment. Tick which jobs' GCs hold each certificate: the renewal then lists every GC to send it to, drafts the email to each one from the certificate's details (you attach the PDF and send it from your own mail), and each pay app says whether its GC has the certificate on file. Type what each job's subcontract requires (coverages, minimum limits, additional insured, waiver of subrogation, primary and non-contributory, whether an umbrella may count), or read it from the subcontract's insurance exhibit PDF in your browser, each value shown with the sentence it came from for you to check, and each requirement shows as met or as a gap in words, on the job and on its draft pay app. It checks what you typed from the certificate, not the policy itself
- Keep your other compliance papers beside them: contractor's licenses by state with class and number, business license, W-9 (the date you signed it; the tax ID number is never a typed field), bonding letter, safety program, EMR letter, OSHA 300A summary and DBE/MBE/WBE certifications. Keep each one's file with it (the license card, the bonding letter PDF, and the signed W-9 only if you choose) and add it to a pay application's backup in one click. The same 30-day note and pay app warning when one with an expiry date is about to lapse, and the whole list as text to paste into a GC's prequalification form. It reads what you type and does not check a license with the state board
- One PDF to send the GC: the application, an index of every attached file and the page it starts on, then the PDF and photo backup, every page numbered (files a PDF can't hold, like spreadsheets, are listed to send separately); change orders get the same packet with their pricing backup

Built · in testing

## Retainage, held and released

Retainage terms come from your contract, not from us. You set the rate per job, separately for work and for stored materials, and every pay app applies it.

- Release a share of what is held (say 50% at substantial completion, or 100% on the final billing) or the dollar amount the GC approved, across all lines, the finished lines or the ones you pick; it is split by what each line holds and totals to the cent
- Retainage held to date, per job and across all jobs, and since when
- Jobs whose work is complete with retainage still held, flagged so you bill it

Built · in testing

## Change orders

Approved change orders add to or deduct from existing lines, or create new ones, and flow into the next pay app, counted in the period they were approved so the summary page matches the GC's records.

- The change-order log per job, with approval dates

Built · in testing

## RFIs and the extra work they lead to

Log each request for information you send the GC on a job: the question, the sheet or spec section it is about, your proposed solution, the date sent and the date you need an answer by. Each one prints as a PDF to attach, with a blank box for the response, and the answer is recorded with who gave it and when.

- Numbered per job, with open, overdue and answered at a glance, how many days each has waited and how long answers take on that job
- Mark whether an answer changes the price or the contract time; an answered RFI that does, with no change order linked, is flagged so the extra work gets priced and billed
- An email draft to the GC's project manager to send an RFI, or to chase one past its response date; you send it from your own mail
- The whole log as a CSV, every plan

Built · in testing

## What you're owed, across every job

One report of every application sent: billed, paid, still owed and retainage held, sorted by money owed, as a page and a CSV.

- Record each check or transfer against an application, including partial payments; it turns paid when the payments reach the certified amount
- Due dates from each subcontract's pay terms (net days, days after the period end, or pay-when-paid with its outer limit): what is past due, and what to expect in the next 30 days
- Aged 0-30, 31-60, 61-90 and 90+ days, with the most overdue application named so you know who to call
- Each GC's billing cutoff ("by the 25th"): a reminder the week before when nothing has gone out yet, and a note when a draft missed it, so an application doesn't slip to next month's draw

Built · in testing

## Lien waivers per pay app

Track the waiver each payment needs (conditional or unconditional, progress or final), prefilled from the job and the amount, and marked sent. Crew plan and up.

- Prints the state's statutory form where we have checked the text against the statute: Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Michigan, Mississippi, Nevada, Texas, Utah and Wyoming, plus Missouri's residential final waiver and Massachusetts' partial waiver and subordination of lien (its pay-app lines filled from the application); a general form in states with no statutory form
- Once a payment arrives, a reminder for the unconditional waiver you now owe, for the amount actually paid
- The lien deadline on every job (every plan): the last day to record a mechanics lien in Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Texas or Washington, from the property's state and your last day on site, with the statute cited, and a warning on the cash page and in the weekly email 45 days ahead on any job that still owes you money
- Preliminary notices from the job page where the statute sets the wording or contents: California (private works), Florida's Notice to Owner, Texas' notices of claim and Wyoming so far, prefilled from the job
- Texas: the § 53.056 notice of claim for unpaid labor or materials and the § 53.057 notice of claim for unpaid retainage, word for word, with the 15th-of-the-month date for each unpaid month (rolled past weekends and Texas legal holidays), the retainage notice's 30 days and the lien affidavit dates; the months read from the job's unpaid pay apps, a log of each notice sent, and a reminder on the cash page and in the weekly email before each month's date
- Florida: the § 713.06 Notice to Owner word for word, with the 45-day last day to serve it and the 40-day last day to mail it so service counts on mailing (§ 713.18), from the day you first furnished work; record each notice and copy served (owner, contractor, the notice of commencement's designee) with how and when it went, see when each counts as served, and get a reminder on the cash page and in the weekly email until the owner has one
- California: record each preliminary notice you give, see the 20-day deadline from the day you first furnished work, get a reminder until the owner and GC have one, print the § 8118 proof of notice declaration, and keep the mailing receipt and return receipt with each notice
- We don't tell you which waiver to sign or what it means for your rights: that is a question for your attorney

Built · in testing

## QuickBooks Online

Send each pay app to QuickBooks Online as an invoice to the GC, with retainage on its own line to a retainage receivable account, so receivables match what you billed. Crew plan and up.

- Payments you record are applied to that invoice in QuickBooks, after checking its open balance matches
- A backcharge or short pay you close out goes over as a credit memo on that invoice, so the aging in QuickBooks matches yours
- Your own items, per job or per line, and on QuickBooks Plus or Advanced the job's class and location, so the profit and loss runs by job type or division
- Sent once: a retry finds the invoice instead of making a second one
- Only connected when an admin asks for it, and you can disconnect it at any time

Built · in testing

## Your office, with roles

Invite your office manager, project managers or bookkeeper by email as admin, editor or viewer.

- Viewers can read and download; editors prepare pay apps; admins manage billing and people

Built · in testing

## Job cost and WIP, from the same numbers

Give each schedule-of-values line a cost budget from your bid, then enter or paste costs as they come in (payroll, supplier invoices, rentals, lower-tier subs), or import the bills, checks and card charges your bookkeeper already tagged to the job in QuickBooks Online. Job cost sits next to what you have billed, so you see an under-billed line before the month closes.

- Budget, cost to date and what is left on every line, with cost percent next to billed percent
- Each line's budget split into labor, material, equipment, subcontract and other, against the costs entered in each, so labor running over shows even when the line total looks fine
- When a line's budget no longer holds, the project manager types a cost to complete and the estimate, percent complete and projected profit follow it
- Purchase orders and lower-tier subcontracts per job: put each invoice against one, see what is still open, and the estimate never drops below cost plus open commitments
- A WIP schedule across your jobs: percent complete by cost, earned revenue, over and under billing, projected gross profit
- CSV for your accountant and a PDF of the WIP schedule for your surety or bank; it is a working schedule, not a financial statement
- Crew plan and up

Built · in testing

## Certified payroll for Davis-Bacon jobs

On a Federal or federally assisted job you owe the GC a certified payroll every week. Type the week's crew once, with each worker's hours by day, rates, fringe credit and deductions, and download it in the columns of the Department of Labor's optional Form WH-347 (Rev. January 2025) with the statement of compliance in the form's own words, ready to sign.

- Hours, fringe credit (6B), cash in lieu (6C), deduction totals and net pay worked out for you; a worker in two classifications gets a row for each under one entry number
- Checks before you print: a full Social Security number (DOL says never), more than 24 hours in a day, deductions over gross, more than 40 straight-time hours, an overtime rate under time and a half, a rate under the wage determination's rate you typed
- Apprenticeship programs and fringe benefit plans on page 2, with an addendum page when they run over
- Fill the week's hours from a time report (QuickBooks time activities, a time-card export from Gusto, ADP or Paychex): each day's straight time and overtime on its day, workers matched by name, read in your browser
- California public works: the same week as the DIR eCPR XML file (schema 2.0, which DIR requires from 13 January 2027) for the Public Works portal, with doubletime, the craft, the apprentice period, fringe by DIR category and deductions split into federal and state tax, SDI, dues and the rest; checked against DIR's rules before you download it. Full SSNs are typed for that file only and never leave your browser
- New York public work: the same week as the NYSDOL Certified Payroll portal's bulk-upload XML (required for Article 8 public work since 1 January 2026), with each row's classification picked from NYSDOL's list and supplements by NYSDOL type
- Washington public works: the same week as the XML file for L&I's PWIA upload, with L&I's trade code and county per row, apprentice registration and step, fringe in L&I's benefit fields and double time apart; full SSNs are typed for that file only and never leave your browser
- Next week starts from this week's crew; workers' names and ID numbers stay in your browser and the download, never on our servers
- Every plan. Not a Department of Labor product and not legal advice: you check the figures and sign

Built · in testing

## A submittal log that warns before a lead time bites

Shop drawings, product data and samples have to come back approved before you can release material. Log each one per job with its spec section, the day it went, the day the GC owes it back and what they stamped on it, and add the date the material is needed on site with its lead time: the log works back the last day to send it and flags the ones that are already late.

- Numbered per job, with the spec section, the type and the GC's own number
- Start the log from the GC's register (spreadsheet, CSV or PDF) or from your spec sections, including a federal spec's SD lists: read in your browser into rows, each shown with where it came from, for you to check and add
- Sent, required back and returned dates; approved, approved as noted, revise and resubmit, rejected or received for record
- Resubmit adds the next revision and keeps the first one's dates on the log
- Flags: overdue back from the GC, late to send, and delivery at risk from the needed-on-site date, lead time and review days you type
- A transmittal cover sheet PDF per submittal: to and from, what is enclosed, the action requested, the return-by date and the needed-on-site date, the revision it replaces, and a box for the reviewer's stamp
- Read the stamp: the action and date filled in from the stamped copy the reviewer returns (a Bluebeam or Acrobat stamp, or one printed on the page), for you to check and save
- The log as CSV for the GC's meeting or your PM
- Every plan

Built · in testing

## A punch list that ends in a back-check, not a phone call

At the end of a job the GC walks it and sends a list. Paste it in (one item per line, with the room or area split off), mark each item fixed as the crew finishes it, and send the GC one email asking for a back-check of everything that is ready. When every item that is yours is accepted, the list says so: that is usually what stands between you and your retainage.

- Numbered per job, with the location, who listed it (GC, architect, owner, inspector or your own walk), the date listed and a due date
- Open, overdue, fixed and awaiting back-check, accepted; or not ours, with the reason (another trade's work, built as drawn), kept out of the count
- A pasted list read line by line: numbering dropped and the location taken from the text before " - " or ": "
- One back-check email to the GC's project manager listing every fixed item, with how many are still open
- The list as a PDF to bring to the walk (all items, or only what is left), with a column for the GC's initials, and as CSV
- Every plan

Built · in testing

## Close-out documents, and what still holds your retainage

Retainage waits on close-out: the punch list accepted and the warranty, O&M manuals, as-builts and the rest delivered. Start from the standard list (consent of surety added on a bonded job), edit it to what your subcontract asks for, and mark each document sent and then accepted. The job page reads the checklist with the punch list and the retainage on your latest pay application and lists what still stands in the way; once nothing does, it drafts the email asking the GC to release it.

- Warranty, O&M manuals, as-builts, attic stock, final inspection and final waiver in one click, with no duplicates; any other document typed in, with where the requirement comes from
- To send, overdue, sent and awaiting the GC, accepted; or not required, with the reason, kept out of the count
- The retainage held on the latest pay application sent, and whether that application bills the whole contract
- What still stands between the job and its retainage, in words: work left to bill, punch items not accepted, documents not sent
- A release-request email to the GC's project manager listing each document with the dates you entered; it states what was delivered, not that the subcontract's terms are met
- The documents themselves kept with each item (the warranty letter, the O&M manuals, the as-built set, photos of attic stock delivered), and the GC's receipt when it comes back
- One close-out binder PDF: a transmittal listing every document with its dates, an index, then each required document's files in checklist order
- Every plan

Built · in testing

## Daily reports from the job site

When a GC disputes a change order, a delay or a pay application, the question is what happened on site that day. Write one report per job and day: the weather, who was on site and their hours, the work done, delays and the hours they cost, equipment, deliveries, visitors and inspections, safety and notes.

- Crew lines by company and trade, with workers and hours each; man-hours totalled per day and for the job
- Start tomorrow's report from today's crew and equipment, so a foreman types only what changed
- Photos from the phone's camera, delivery tickets and inspection reports kept with the day's report, and the report with its photos as one PDF for the GC
- Every report written, changed or deleted, and every photo added or removed, is in the job history with who did it and when
- Weekdays since the first report with no report are listed, so a missing day is caught while people still remember it; your company's holidays are left out, so Thanksgiving is not a gap
- Each report as a PDF, or a week's or a month's reports in one PDF to send the GC or attach to the pay application
- The whole log as CSV
- Every plan. A daily report is a record, not a notice of delay: your subcontract says how notice must be given

Built · in testing

## Crew timesheets that land on job cost

Your foreman knows who worked where; job cost usually finds out after payroll, weeks later. Enter each worker's hours by day on a job and a schedule-of-values line, and post the week: the labor goes on each job's costs, so an over-running line shows while it can still be fixed.

- Your crew list with each worker's trade and hourly rate; a worker with past hours is made inactive, not deleted
- One week per screen, a row per job and line, hours by day; your company's workweek (Monday or any other day) is kept fixed once hours are entered
- Overtime past 40 hours in the workweek at time and a half, on the hours worked after the 40th, so the job worked on Saturday carries it
- Post to job costs: one labor cost per job and line, wages plus the burden percent you type (none is assumed); a week posted twice adds nothing
- A payroll CSV (straight time, overtime, rate and gross per worker) for your payroll service
- On a prevailing-wage job, one button on the certified payroll page fills the WH-347 week from these hours: straight time, overtime and each worker's trade, with any hours on other jobs named for the gross
- Hours on every plan; posting them to job costs comes with job costing (Crew and up). Federal overtime only: state daily overtime, double time and prevailing wages are for your payroll service

Built · in testing

## Your schedule on each job, and the lookahead for the GC's meeting

List the activities you plan on a job (rough-in level 2, set fixtures, pull wire to the panel) with the crew doing each, its start and finish, how far along it is and the activity it waits for. Bring the three-week lookahead to the GC's coordination meeting as a PDF, and see every crew across every job for the Monday crew meeting.

- Each activity's status for today: not started, in progress, done, late start or past its finish, from the dates you typed
- An activity that starts before the one it waits for finishes is flagged, with the earliest day it can start
- When the GC's schedule slips, move an activity and everything waiting on it by workdays in one step; finished work stays where it happened
- Your company's holidays left out of every workday count, move and lookahead: type the days you take off, or start from the federal list and delete the ones your crews work
- A crew lookahead across every active job, grouped by the crew typed on each activity, listing the days a crew has work on two jobs
- The lookahead as a PDF (three or six weeks) and the whole schedule as CSV
- Delays by activity: a daily report names the activity its lost hours held up, and the delay log (days, hours, the delay as written) prints as a PDF and attaches to a time-extension change order as backup
- Every plan. Your schedule here does not change the contract or the GC's schedule, and the delay log is not a notice of delay

Built · in testing

## Estimates and proposals that become the job

Price the bid from cost lines (labor, material, equipment, subcontract, other) rolled up into bid items, with markup set per category and sales tax on material. Send the GC a proposal PDF, and when you win, the bid starts the job: its bid items become the schedule of values you bill against.

- Bring in the bid sheet you already keep: an .xlsx or CSV, a supplier's quote, a takeoff material list, or rows pasted from Excel or Google Sheets. It is read in your browser and never uploaded
- Columns are found by their headers, a unit cost per category (material, labor, equipment, sub) gives one line each, and totals and unreadable rows are left out with the reason
- Nothing is guessed: a line with no price comes in at $0 and is marked to be priced, and a unit cost worked out from a total is marked for you to check
- A company price list: material prices, labor and equipment rates and sub quotes typed once, or read from a supplier's price sheet, and picked into any estimate. Save an estimate's lines to the list, and bring an older bid up to the list's prices before you send it
- Add and deduct alternates, numbered on the proposal with a box for the GC to tick; when you win, the accepted ones decide the job's schedule of values
- The proposal shows prices only, with includes, excludes, the date it lapses and an acceptance block; your costs and markup stay yours
- Won bids carry each item's cost to the job's budget on plans with job costing, split by labor, material (with its tax), equipment and subcontract as you bid it
- Every plan

Built · in testing

## T&M tickets signed on site, billed as a change order

Extra work the GC's superintendent asks for gets paid when there is a ticket written up that day, signed on site, priced and sent as a change order before the subcontract's deadline. Write the ticket on a phone: the work, the location, who directed it, and the labor, material and equipment that went in. Hand the phone over to sign, then price it in the office and bill one ticket or a month of them on a single change order.

- Labor by trade with workers and hours, material with quantities and units, equipment hours; rates can wait until the office prices it
- The GC's representative signs on the screen (or on paper); once signed, the work and the quantities are locked, and rates and markups can still be set
- Labor, material and equipment markups, each on its own subtotal, carried to the next ticket; rates already used on the job fill in on request
- A rate sheet per job from the subcontract's T&M terms (labor by trade, equipment, material, markups), drafted from the job's tickets in one click; a ticket priced off the sheet says so before it goes to the GC
- Signed tickets not on a change order yet are listed in the weekly money-to-chase email, job by job, with the oldest work date
- Signed, priced tickets become one pending change order on an existing or new schedule-of-values line, and count in pay apps once the GC approves it
- The job's headline figure: signed work not yet on a change order, with the oldest ticket's date
- A priced PDF with the signature, a field copy to sign by hand, every ticket on a change order as one backup PDF, and the log as CSV
- Every plan. A signed ticket is a record of the work, not an approved change order: your subcontract says how extra work is authorized and billed

Built · in testing

## Lower-tier waivers from your suppliers and sub-subs

Many GCs hold a payment until your own suppliers and sub-subcontractors have signed lien waivers for the work in your application. Each pay app keeps the list of who owes you one, what for and through when, and whether you have asked and when it came in, so the application goes out with every waiver the GC asked for.

- Who to ask comes from the job's purchase orders and subcontracts (ticked when they have invoiced something) and from last month's list
- Each waiver is owed, asked (with the days waiting) or received, with the amount and a note
- A short request to copy or open as an email: the job, the GC, the waiver kind, the through date and the amount
- The pay app says how many are in and names who is still out
- Attach the signed copy on its row: marked received, and named for the supplier in the backup packet
- Every waiver still out, across all your open jobs, on the projects page and in the weekly email, longest wait first
- Crew plan and up, with lien waivers. Which waivers a contract or state requires is yours to check; nothing is sent for you

Built · in testing

## Your GC's portal, filled from the pay app

Each GC has its own portal, cut-off date and format, and the numbers get typed in again once per GC. The pay app you already built fills the files and figures the common portals take, so the portal matches the G702/G703 you send.

- Procore: the subcontractor SOV template filled from your lines, and each month's invoice amounts by line or totalled under the GC's own SOV positions
- Oracle Textura: the This Period or To Date billing upload template, downloaded from Textura and given back filled
- GCPay: the schedule of values as the Excel file its Upload button takes, lump-sum or unit-price
- Trimble Pay: the Flashtract template from its Bulk upload, given back with your lines in columns A to C and its header rows untouched, checked against the contract value
- Each job's billing cutoff ("by the 25th"), with a reminder the week before when nothing has gone out
- Built from each portal's published help, not yet tried on a live project. Submitting into the portal stays your step: we prepare the numbers and files

Next

## Also next

In the order subcontractors ask for them:

- A saved checklist per GC: the attachments and format each GC wants, so every pay app for that GC starts with them
- More portals (Siteline and others) when subcontractors bill through them

## What it won't do

- Give legal advice, interpret your contract or tell you which lien waiver to sign.

- Produce AIA Contract Documents. If your GC requires the AIA's own forms, you still use those.

- Promise faster payment. It can help you send a complete, correct pay app on time; when you get paid is up to your GC and owner.

PayApps is not affiliated with the American Institute of Architects (AIA) and does not produce AIA Contract Documents. Nothing on this site is legal advice.

[Start free on one job](https://payapps.marisstella.app/?signup&from=payapps-site%2Ffeatures)

Pricing

# Simple monthly plans, sized by active jobs

Start free on one job, no card. Paid plans add jobs, users, lien waivers and QuickBooks Online; they are not on sale yet.

## Free

$0 / month

1 active job · 1 user

Try it on one real job, start to finish.

- Schedule of values, change orders and retainage
- Pay application summary and continuation sheet as PDF and CSV
- 250 MB of attached backup and photos

## Solo

$99 / month

or $1,069 a year

5 active jobs · 2 users

For an owner who does the billing after the crew goes home.

- Everything in Free
- 5 GB of attachments

## Crew

$179 / month

or $1,933 a year

20 active jobs · 3 users

For a shop with an office manager billing several GCs every month.

- Everything in Solo
- Lien waivers per pay app, with statutory forms where verified
- QuickBooks Online: pay apps as invoices with retainage, payments applied
- Job cost per line and a WIP schedule (over/under billing, projected profit)
- 20 GB of attachments

## Company

$249 / month

or $2,689 a year

unlimited active jobs · unlimited users

For a subcontractor with project managers and a billing team.

- Everything in Crew
- 50 GB of attachments

Prices in US dollars, before any sales tax. No setup fee; cancel any time, and a full refund within 30 days of your first paid payment ([Refund Policy](https://marisstella.app/payapps/refunds)). The [features page](https://marisstella.app/payapps/features) marks what is built and what comes next.

## Questions about pricing

### Can I buy a paid plan today?

Not yet. The Free plan is open now with no card and no time limit. These are the prices the app is set up to charge when paid plans go on sale; if they change before then we will say so here first, and you choose whether to subscribe.

### What is an active job?

A job you haven't closed. When a job is finished, close it and its slot frees up; its pay apps, waivers and files stay in your account to read and download on every plan.

### What happens if I downgrade or stop paying?

Nothing is hidden or deleted. You can still read, export and download everything on every job. Starting new pay apps or jobs past the Free limits needs a paid plan again.

### Why price by jobs and not by contract value?

Our costs grow with the number of jobs we help you set up and bill, not with their dollar value, and a flat monthly price is easier to plan for than a percentage of what you bill.

### Is there an annual price?

Yes: each paid plan is also offered yearly at 10% off twelve months.

### How were these prices set?

Cost-plus: each paid plan is priced at 1.8 to 2 times what it costs us to serve a customer who uses all of it. Most of that cost is support time, helping set up schedules of values and answering why a total doesn't match the GC's; the rest is hosting, file storage and payment fees.

[Start free on one job](https://payapps.marisstella.app/?signup&from=payapps-site%2Fpricing)

# Terms of Service

Version 2026-11-27 · Maris Stella Labs LLC. This is the same text the [app](https://payapps.marisstella.app/legal/terms) asks every account to accept.

## 1. Who we are

PayApps (the "Service") is operated by **Maris Stella Labs LLC**, a Colorado limited liability company ("we", "us"). These Terms are an agreement between us and the company that creates an account (the "Customer", "you"). The person who accepts these Terms confirms they are authorized to do so on the company's behalf.

## 2. The Service

The Service helps contractors prepare and track monthly pay applications: schedules of values, change orders, retainage, application summaries and continuation sheets (as PDF and CSV), lien waiver tracking and printable waiver forms, and reports on money owed and retainage held. It also keeps the job records around billing: estimates, job costs and commitments, a job schedule, RFIs, submittals, daily reports, time-and-material tickets, punch lists, close-out documents, insurance certificates and company documents, files you attach to them, certified payroll PDFs, and, if your admin connects it, invoices sent to and costs read from QuickBooks Online.

## 3. You are the one billing

The Service does the arithmetic from the figures **you enter**. It does not know your contract, your general contractor's requirements or the work you performed. Before you send anything, you are responsible for checking every figure, and for making sure each application, waiver and document is accurate, complete and in the form your contract and the law require. General contractors, owners, lenders and sureties may rely on what you send; they rely on you, not on us.

- **Not an AIA document.** Our application summary and continuation sheet use our own layout. They are not AIA Contract Documents® forms (G702/G703) and are not endorsed by the American Institute of Architects. If your contract requires the AIA forms themselves, use them.
- **Lien waivers are not legal advice.** Where we print a state's statutory waiver form, we reproduce the text we verified against the state's published statute. Statutes change, and the effect of signing a waiver depends on your facts. We do not tell you whether to sign, which form applies, or what rights you keep. Ask a construction lawyer when it matters.
- **Certified payroll is yours to certify.** The certified payroll page checks the arithmetic of the week you type and prints it; it does not know the prevailing wage rates that apply to your job, and it does not file anything. You and your certifying official are responsible for the rates, the classifications and the statement of compliance you sign and submit.
- **Insurance checks are a comparison, not insurance advice.** Where the Service compares a certificate with the limits and endorsements you entered as your subcontract's requirements, it compares only what you typed. Your policy, your broker and your contract decide what is covered.
- **Dates and reminders come from what you enter.** Deadlines, renewal dates and "to chase" lists are worked out from the dates you type; the Service does not know your contract's notice periods unless you enter them, and a missed reminder does not change any deadline.
- **No legal, tax or accounting advice.** Nothing in the Service is legal, tax, accounting or financial advice.

## 4. Accounts and sign-in

You sign in with email and password. Keep your credentials secure and tell us promptly about any unauthorized use. Your company's admins decide who has access and with what role (admin, editor or viewer). You are responsible for activity under your company's accounts.

## 5. Plans, fees and billing

- **Plans.** A free plan covers one active job. Paid plans and their prices and limits are shown in the app before you buy.
- **Merchant of record.** Payments are processed by a third-party merchant of record (Paddle). The merchant of record is the seller of record for your purchase, handles payment, invoicing and applicable sales tax, and its own terms apply to the payment transaction.
- **Plan changes.** You can upgrade, downgrade or cancel at any time from the billing page. Changes take effect as described in the app. If we change prices, we will tell you in advance and the change applies from your next billing period.
- **After a downgrade** you can still read and print everything you created; creating or changing items beyond the free plan's limits needs a paid plan.
- **Refunds** are covered by the Refund Policy.

## 6. Acceptable use

You agree to follow the Acceptable Use Policy. In particular, you will not use the Service to prepare false or inflated applications or waivers.

## 7. Your content

- **You own your content**: jobs, schedules of values, change orders, applications, waivers and everything else you enter.
- You give us a limited, non-exclusive license to host, copy, process and transmit your content **only as needed to provide, secure and support the Service** for you. This license ends when your content is deleted.
- We do not sell your content, use it for advertising, or share it with other customers. See the Privacy Policy.

## 8. Confidentiality

We treat your non-public content, including contract sums and billing figures, as confidential. We use it only to provide the Service, share it only with the subprocessors listed in the Privacy Policy who need it to provide the Service, and protect it with reasonable safeguards. We may disclose information if required by law, and will tell you first where we lawfully can.

## 9. Availability

We work to keep the Service available, but it may be interrupted for maintenance or by events outside our control. Keep your own copies (PDF and CSV exports) of anything you have sent or must keep.

## 10. Termination

You may stop using the Service and cancel at any time. We may suspend or terminate accounts that violate these Terms or the Acceptable Use Policy, or for non-payment, with notice where practical. Before your account closes, you can download your applications as PDF and CSV.

## 11. Disclaimers

The Service is provided "as is" and "as available". To the extent the law allows, we disclaim implied warranties, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose and non-infringement. Nothing in these Terms limits rights you have under law that cannot be waived.

## 12. Limitation of liability

To the extent the law allows, neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, or for lost payments, profits, lien rights or data. Our total liability for any claim relating to the Service is limited to the **fees you paid us in the 12 months before the claim arose**.

## 13. Changes to these Terms

We may update these Terms. We will post the new version with a new version date and, for material changes, notify account admins in advance. You will be asked to accept the new version the next time you sign in.

## 14. Governing law

These Terms are governed by the laws of the **State of Colorado**, USA, without regard to conflict-of-law rules. Courts located in Colorado have jurisdiction over disputes, unless the law requires otherwise.

## 15. Contact

# Refund Policy

Version 2026-11-26 · Maris Stella Labs LLC. This is the same text the [app](https://payapps.marisstella.app/legal/refunds) asks every account to accept.

## Try it free first

PayApps has a free plan for one active job, with no card required, so you can build a real pay application before you pay.

## 30-day money-back guarantee

If a paid plan is not right for your company, you can request a **full refund within 30 days** of your first paid subscription payment.

## How to request a refund

- Contact us, or reply to the receipt from our merchant of record (Paddle). Tell us which company the subscription is for.
- Refunds are issued through the merchant of record to the original payment method, including any sales tax charged.
- Refunds usually appear within 5–10 business days, depending on your bank.

## After the first 30 days

- You can cancel at any time. Cancellation stops future renewals; you keep the paid plan until the end of the period you paid for, then the free plan's limits apply. Everything you created stays readable and printable.
- Renewals after the first 30 days are generally not refundable, except where required by law or in cases of billing error or an extended outage, which we will review in good faith.

## Plan changes

When you change plans, any credit or charge is handled as shown at checkout.

# Acceptable Use Policy

Version 2026-11-26 · Maris Stella Labs LLC. This is the same text the [app](https://payapps.marisstella.app/legal/acceptable-use) asks every account to accept.

PayApps exists to help contractors bill accurately and get paid for the work they did. You agree not to use it to do any of the following.

## Honest billing

- Prepare applications, change orders or waivers that are **false or inflated**, such as billing for work not performed or materials not stored, or misstating retainage or payments received.
- Prepare a document for a company you are not authorized to represent, or impersonate another person or company.
- Present our application summary or continuation sheet as an AIA Contract Documents® form.

## Other people's data

- Enter personal information about others unless you have the right to share it with us for this purpose.
- Invite people to your company who should not see its billing records.

## The Service

- Attempt to access another company's data, probe for vulnerabilities, or bypass access controls or plan limits.
- Overload the Service, or use it to send spam (including invitation emails to people who did not ask for them).
- Resell or share access outside your company without our agreement.

## Enforcement

We may suspend or terminate accounts that violate this policy, with notice where practical. Report misuse or security issues to us.

## Contact

Maris Stella Labs LLC, Colorado, USA · [hello@marisstella.app](mailto:hello@marisstella.app)
